title: Lesson Plan — Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom + A Tiger in the Zoo (Class 10 CBSE English)
subject: English
chapter_title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
objectives: Recall the events of Mandela's inauguration and the basic timeline of his life.
Explain apartheid and the long South African struggle against it.
Discuss Mandela's ideas — twin obligations, courage, love, freedom.
Analyse the structure and contrasts of 'A Tiger in the Zoo'.
Connect the two pieces as a meditation on FREEDOM at every scale.
Use new vocabulary from the chapter.
prerequisites: Some familiarity with the words 'democracy', 'segregation', 'civil rights' from earlier classes.
Knowledge of basic literary terms — speaker, image, contrast, rhyme.
Comfort reading and discussing in groups.
materials: World map (to locate South Africa) + photo of Mandela's inauguration
Timeline strip 1948 → 2013 with key dates of Mandela's life
Vocabulary flashcards (apartheid, ANC, Robben Island, ubuntu, lurks, snarls, terrorises)

activities.description: Hook: 'What does FREEDOM mean to you?' Take 3-4 responses; show a picture of Mandela's inauguration; promise the chapter will explore freedom from two sides.
student_actions: Note one question of their own.

activities.description: Place Mandela's life on a timeline (1918 birth → 1948 apartheid → 1964 imprisoned → 1990 released → 1994 inauguration → 2013 death). Students fill in events as a group.

Cover four blocks: (i) Mandela's inauguration day — what happened, why it mattered; (ii) Apartheid background and Mandela's political life; (iii) Mandela's key ideas — twin obligations, courage, love, freedom; (iv) 'A Tiger in the Zoo' — alternation of caged + wild scenes, the final image of brilliant stars.
teacher_actions: Read the poem aloud and decode.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering plot, themes, vocabulary, and a short reading on the poem.
Exit ticket: 4 quick questions, one from each block.
Homework: write a 5-line paragraph on 'A small freedom I value'.

homework: Write a 5-line paragraph: 'A small freedom I value'.
Memorise either 'A Tiger in the Zoo' or one paragraph of Mandela's speech and recite tomorrow.
Write 5 sentences using the vocabulary words: apartheid, inauguration, lurks, snarls, terrorises.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on Mandela's idea that the oppressor is as unfree as the oppressed using a 5-point rubric.
Peer-grade the 'small freedom I value' paragraph.
references: NCERT Class 10 — First Flight, Chapter 2: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom + A Tiger in the Zoo.
